external_spec_note: The double-counting defect and its fix follow directly from settleAccount's own source; no protocol/business convention beyond the source is needed to justify the relation.
case_notes: Fixed18Lib._from/.add/.sign/.abs and UFixed18Lib arithmetic are load-bearing (Step 1: the relation's derived constant depends on ordinary signed-fixed-point add/sign/abs semantics) but are a generic, protocol-independent fixed-point math library (same category as SafeMath/PRBMath in §6 Step 2) — recorded as a case note, not counted under Additional functions/contracts or Context breadth.
extraction_note: Attached at the buggy statement `self.shortfall = self.shortfall.add(shortfall);` (line 23). Debug seeds in the case JSON (self.shortfall=[100,100], self.balances[account]=[50,50], amount=[-100,-100]) confirm the derivation: newBalance = 50 + (-100) = -50 (negative) => local named-return `shortfall` = self.shortfall(100).add(newBalance.abs()=50) = 150; the buggy code then double-counts by computing self.shortfall = self.shortfall(100).add(shortfall=150) = 250, whereas the intended fix is a plain `self.shortfall = shortfall;` (=150), since `shortfall` already incorporates the prior self.shortfall value. Judgment call: excluded the mapping key `account` as a standalone program value (same rationale as the loop index/key exclusion in §6 — only the value self.balances[account] produces is relevant to this relation, not which specific address it is) while still counting the container `self.balances` itself. Judgment call: classified Value-level because the defect is an extra/wrong operand within one otherwise-complete assignment expression (self.shortfall.add(shortfall) vs. the intended bare `shortfall`), not a missing distinct processing step. Did not use annotation_plans.md for the annotation text (used the case JSON directly per instructions); consulted it only for bug background, and it does not contradict this reading.
